market_summary: AI-trade momentum remains strong post-NVDA earnings beat; existing portfolio positions are flat and not worth churning, but the book lacks NVDA exposure.
memo:
## Research Memo — Portfolio Review & Trade Decision

**Account snapshot:** $899.69 of the $1,000 CHF budget is already deployed across AMZN, GOOGL, META, MSFT, and SPY. All five positions are essentially flat (P&L ranging from -0.3% to +0.3%), meaning there is no urgency to trim losers or take profits — these are noise-level moves, not trend signals. Only $100.31 remains to deploy.

**Market read:** The tape has been driven almost entirely by the AI trade this cycle. Nvidia's print was the standout catalyst — 
Wall Street welcomed the report, and Nvidia stock rose after the release and during the conference call, with other AI-trade stocks also getting a boost
. Ahead of the print, sell-side was already leaning bullish: 
Stifel's Ruben Roy raised his price target on Nvidia to $250 from $212 ahead of earnings, implying nearly 38% upside
, and current consensus sits even higher — 
NVDA's average 12-month analyst price target is around $304.67
. Broader risk appetite has been supportive too: 
both SPY and QQQ closed higher as AI stocks surged, aided by a cooler PCE inflation report
. The headline flow (Hugging Face acquisition, Jensen Huang's "compute is revenue" commentary, Cramer/analysts flagging further upside) reinforces that the AI infrastructure trade still has momentum, not exhaustion.

**Positions held (AMZN, GOOGL, META, MSFT, SPY):** No action warranted. Moves are sub-1%, well inside normal noise, and selling here would just realize trading costs for no informational edge. Holding is free — churning small, flat positions is not.

**Gap in the book:** Despite five mega-cap/index names, the portfolio has zero direct NVDA exposure — the single stock most central to the current earnings-driven AI rally. With only $100.31 of dry powder left in the 1,000 CHF budget, this is the highest-conviction, lowest-cost way to use remaining capital rather than force a rebalance of already-fine positions.

**Trade recommendation:**
- **BUY NVDA, ~$95** (leaves a small buffer under the 1,000 CHF cap). Thesis: fresh earnings beat, raised price targets (~$250–$305 range vs. current levels), and confirmed AI-capex momentum (Hugging Face deal, Huang's bullish commentary) — this is a decisive, catalyst-backed edge, unlike simply nudging the existing flat positions.
- **HOLD** AMZN, GOOGL, META, MSFT, SPY unchanged — P&L is immaterial and no news justifies trimming or adding.
- **No sells** — nothing in the book is a loser worth cutting or a winner worth harvesting at this size.

**Bottom line:** Deploy the remaining ~$100.31 into a single NVDA buy to close the portfolio's exposure gap to the current AI-earnings catalyst; leave all existing positions untouched this cycle to avoid unnecessary trading costs on flat P&L.

orders.reasoning: Deploy remaining budget into NVDA to capture AI-earnings catalyst momentum and close portfolio's exposure gap, per analyst memo.
